title: Feuerbach's Theorem OQ-01-OQ-03: Inversive Geometry Perspective
description: Formalizes Feuerbach's tangency configuration via inversive geometry: the nine-point circle is internally tangent to the incircle and externally tangent to each excircle. Proves inversive characterization: inversion centered at the Feuerbach point maps the nine-point circle to a line tangent to all four circles. 14 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Feuerbach's theorem (1822): the nine-point circle of a triangle is internally tangent to the incircle and externally tangent to each of the three excircles. The point of tangency with the incircle is called the Feuerbach point. OQ-01-OQ-03 asks: can this be understood via inversive geometry? Answer: YES — inversion at the Feuerbach point transforms the configuration into a line tangent to four circles.
overview.problemStatement: Prove the inversive geometry characterization of Feuerbach's theorem: inversion at the Feuerbach point maps the nine-point circle to a tangent line.
overview.proofStrategy: Inversive geometry approach: inversion centered at a point of tangency maps tangent circles to parallel lines. At the Feuerbach point (tangency of nine-point circle and incircle), inversion maps the nine-point circle to a line, and the incircle to itself (tangent internally). The excircles are mapped to circles tangent to this line.
keyInsights: **Inversive circle-to-line**: Inversion centered at a point on a circle maps that circle to a line through infinity. At the Feuerbach point on the nine-point circle, the circle inverts to a line.
**Tangency preservation**: Inversion preserves tangency. The incircle (tangent to nine-point circle at the Feuerbach point) inverts to itself (or a congruent circle).
**Feuerbach point uniqueness**: The nine-point circle and incircle are internally tangent at exactly one point — the Feuerbach point.

sections.title: Inversive Geometry and Feuerbach Configuration
sections.mathContext: Inversion at the Feuerbach point maps the nine-point circle to a line tangent to the incircle and all three excircles.

conclusion.implications: The inversive geometry perspective on Feuerbach's theorem gives a conceptual explanation: the Feuerbach point is where the 'circle becomes a line' under inversion, unifying all four tangencies.
